processes.title: Sales Inquiry
processes.memory_hook: Customer asks. We qualify before we promise.
processes.business_intent: Capture an early customer request before a formal quotation or order exists, preserving requirements and follow-on traceability without creating a fulfillment commitment.

control_plane.why: define how long the request remains commercially relevant
control what is copied into quotation or order
separate active opportunities from closed requests

data_hinges.changes: what later quotation or order must solve
whether the inquiry remains usable
partner, pricing and sales-area context for follow-on documents

impact_summary: No inventory or accounting movement occurs; the value is preserving demand context before a formal commercial promise is made.
constraints: Do not turn every vague customer conversation into ERP master data or a sales document.
CRM/Sales Cloud may own opportunity qualification while S/4HANA owns the transactional inquiry.
lead_questions: Which information belongs in CRM versus S/4?
When should an inquiry become a quotation?
What must be copied and what should be redetermined later?

processes.title: Sales with One-Time Customer
processes.memory_hook: Sell once without pretending the buyer deserves a permanent master record.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Order Entry with One-Time Customer

processes.business_intent: Run a normal sales transaction for an occasional buyer while entering transaction-specific address and partner information instead of maintaining a dedicated customer master for every one-off sale.

control_plane.why: provides the reusable account shell
stores the actual buyer details for this transaction
ensures the temporary partner context still produces valid billing and FI documents

data_hinges.changes: shipping, taxation and output recipient
tax determination and legal invoice data
receivables and payment processing

impact_summary: The fulfillment process remains ordinary, but master-data governance moves from a permanent customer record into the transaction.
constraints: Not suitable when repeated business, credit history, contracts, rebates or customer-specific master data are expected.
Duplicate use can become a data-quality loophole if users avoid proper customer onboarding.
lead_questions: When does a one-time buyer become a real customer master?
Which controls prevent duplicate or fraudulent one-time addresses?
How do credit, tax and sanctions checks work for transient partner data?

processes.title: Free Goods Processing
processes.memory_hook: The order has value, but part of the quantity is deliberately free.
processes.business_intent: Grant bonus quantities according to commercial rules while keeping the paid and free quantities explicit in order, delivery and pricing behavior.

control_plane.why: decides eligibility, minimum quantity and bonus quantity
decides whether free quantity is inside or added on top of ordered quantity
keeps bonus items free while preserving logistics

data_hinges.changes: qualification and calculated bonus
whether promotion applies
total delivered quantity and commercial interpretation

impact_summary: Revenue and delivered quantity no longer move one-to-one; logistics must still execute the free quantity correctly.
constraints: Free goods are different from a full free-of-charge order and from a complaint replacement.
Partial delivery and quantity changes can recalculate or redistribute the free quantity.
lead_questions: Is the bonus inside the ordered quantity or additional?
What happens when the customer changes quantity after determination?
How should free quantity affect margin and promotion analytics?

processes.title: Returnables Processing
processes.memory_hook: We sell the goods; the packaging is expected to come back.
processes.business_intent: Track reusable packaging or containers delivered to customers while retaining ownership and expecting later return or settlement.

control_plane.why: separates reusable asset-like packaging from the sold product
tracks company-owned returnables located at the customer
decides whether packaging comes back or is commercially settled

data_hinges.changes: open returnable exposure
physical and financial exposure
pickup or charging decision

impact_summary: Location changes without immediate ownership transfer, similar to consignment logic but for reusable packaging rather than saleable customer stock.
constraints: Requires discipline around customer stock reconciliation; otherwise pallets and containers quietly become a permanent donation program.
Returnables and consignment solve different business objects even though both use customer-located special stock concepts.
lead_questions: Who owns the packaging at each step?
How is overdue returnable stock reconciled or charged?
Can warehouse execution create returnables delivery without a new sales order?

processes.title: Collective Billing and Invoice Lists
processes.memory_hook: Fulfill many times; present the commercial result in fewer documents.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Order Processing with Invoice List and Collective Billing

processes.business_intent: Consolidate multiple billable references into collective billing documents and, where required, group existing billing documents into an invoice list for the customer.

control_plane.why: decide which references can share one billing document
decide which billing documents are grouped for presentation/settlement
provide common header values required for convergence

data_hinges.changes: grouping eligibility
billing split
when invoices enter the list

impact_summary: Physical fulfillment remains unchanged; the process changes document granularity, customer settlement and billing operations.
constraints: Collective billing and invoice lists are not the same: the first merges reference documents into invoices, the second groups already-created billing documents.
Unexpected header differences create billing splits that users often discover only after staring accusingly at the due list.
lead_questions: Are we consolidating deliveries into one invoice or invoices into one invoice list?
Which exact field causes an unwanted billing split?
Does customer accounting require one legal invoice or only one statement-style grouping?

processes.title: Sales Rebate Processing
processes.memory_hook: The price is not finished at invoice time.
processes.business_intent: Manage retrospective customer rebates and bonus agreements using condition contracts, business-volume determination, accruals and periodic/final settlement.

control_plane.why: defines partner, validity, eligible business volume and rebate conditions
decides which transactions contribute to the agreement
control accrual and payment timing

data_hinges.changes: eligible relationship
which billed sales count toward rebate
rebate amount and timing

impact_summary: A sale that was commercially complete at invoice time can still create later liabilities, credits and margin adjustments.
constraints: Settlement Management is broader than classic SD pricing; ownership spans pricing, billing, accounting and contract governance.
Incorrect business-volume criteria can create financially large errors long after the original invoices were posted.
lead_questions: What business volume counts and why?
When is an accrual required?
How do returns and credit memos reduce eligible rebate volume?
Who owns settlement exceptions?

processes.title: Sales Payment Overlays
processes.memory_hook: Same sales flow, different way of proving the customer can pay.
processes.business_intent: Overlay the sales process with payment-instrument or payment-authorization logic such as SEPA direct debit mandates or digital card/payment-service processing.

control_plane.control: payment method / mandate / payment card context
control_plane.why: selects how payment is authorized or collected
connects ERP documents to external payment providers where applicable
carries payment context into receivable and clearing

data_hinges.changes: collection path
whether payment can proceed
external traceability

impact_summary: The order-to-cash documents remain familiar, but payment risk and external integration become part of the process contract.
constraints: Payment capability is localization, provider and deployment sensitive.
Do not confuse payment authorization with credit management; they answer different risk questions.
lead_questions: Who owns payment authorization: S/4, a payment service, or commerce?
What happens when authorization succeeds but order creation fails?
How are refunds linked to the original digital payment?

processes.title: Sales Quantity Contract
processes.memory_hook: We agree the total quantity first; we create call-offs when the customer is ready to consume it.
processes.business_intent: We use a quantity contract when we want a long-term commercial commitment for a defined product quantity without fixing every delivery date and delivery quantity up front.

control_plane.why: we define how much the customer may release and during which period

control_plane.control: contract → order reference and copy control
control_plane.why: we decide which release-order document can consume the contract and how reference data is transferred

control_plane.control: Outline Agrmt Mess. in the order type
control_plane.why: we can let SAP search for an open contract when we create an order without an explicit reference
we control which partners may place call-offs against the agreement
we decide how the process reacts when released quantity reaches or exceeds the commercial target

data_hinges.changes: how much of the commercial commitment remains available
whether a new call-off is still allowed
the operational demand that ATP, scheduling and delivery must execute
which commercial terms we expect to carry into or influence the release order

impact_summary: We keep the long-term quantity commitment in the contract and the executable delivery demand in the release order.
We update contract consumption when release orders reference the contract, so document flow becomes part of the commercial control.
When we need customer prepayment, we can use down-payment processing for sales quantity contracts with a milestone billing plan and release-order delivery blocking.
constraints: We do not treat the quantity contract itself as the normal delivery demand because the contract does not contain the detailed delivery schedule used by the release order.
We test pricing, reference status and quantity updates together; a sales order that looks correct can still leave the contract consumption wrong if the reference design is wrong.
We verify the exact apps, item categories and configuration options against the target S/4HANA deployment and release.
lead_questions: Are we controlling a total quantity or a delivery schedule?
Which order type may release against the contract, and what must copy or redetermine?
How do we find an open contract when the user creates the order without a reference?
What do we want SAP to do when the customer tries to release more than the remaining quantity?
Do we require a down payment before we allow delivery?

processes.title: Sales Value Contract
processes.memory_hook: We agree the money first; every call-off consumes part of the open contract value.
processes.business_intent: We use a value contract when the customer commits to a target monetary value and may release different allowed products or services during the contract period.

control_plane.why: we define the commercial ceiling and the period in which it can be consumed

control_plane.control: allowed product scope and release rules
control_plane.why: we decide which products, hierarchies or agreed selections may be released
we decide who may release against the agreement

control_plane.control: contract → order copy control and pricing
control_plane.why: we control reference eligibility, data transfer and price handling in the release order

control_plane.control: billing plan when we bill the contract directly
control_plane.why: we can bill the value contract itself on planned dates instead of relying only on release-order billing

data_hinges.changes: how much commercial value remains available
the currency in which we measure consumption even when the release order uses another currency
the released-value calculation as orders, deliveries, billing, returns or reversals change
which materials we may release against the agreement

impact_summary: We control consumption by value rather than by physical quantity.
We can create release orders in another currency; SAP converts the value into the contract currency for contract consumption.
We can bill per release order, or we can bill the value contract directly when we use a billing plan.
constraints: We keep quantity-contract and value-contract item logic separate; SAP does not process both item types together in one contract document.
We do not assume the released value is only the original order value because later delivery, billing, return, rejection and reversal events can change the contract consumption.
If we bill the contract directly, we design the billing-plan and later credit/correction process deliberately.
lead_questions: Why do we need value control instead of quantity control?
Which products and partners are allowed to consume the agreement?
Do we bill the release orders or the value contract itself?
Which currency owns the commercial ceiling?
How do returns, cancellations and price changes affect the released value?

processes.title: Sales Scheduling Agreement
processes.memory_hook: We keep the long-term agreement and the delivery schedule in the same operational relationship.
processes.business_intent: We use a sales scheduling agreement when the customer repeatedly supplies concrete delivery requirements over time, so we need schedule lines and delivery schedules rather than separate contract call-off orders.

control_plane.why: we define the long-term sales document and the logistics behavior of its items
we represent the customer's rolling delivery requirements at the required planning horizon
we hold the quantities and dates that drive delivery execution
we reconcile what the customer requested, what we received as a release and what we already delivered
we can receive delivery schedules from the buyer and update the corresponding sales scheduling agreement

data_hinges.changes: what becomes due for delivery and when
the planning horizon and operational precision of customer demand
how we reconcile repeated releases over a long-running agreement
how we identify and execute the customer's recurring demand

impact_summary: We do not need a separate release-order sales order for the normal scheduling-agreement flow because the operational dates and quantities live in the scheduling agreement schedule lines.
We can create deliveries from schedule lines that become due.
For long-running agreements, we watch document-flow volume because years of follow-on documents can affect performance.
constraints: We distinguish sales scheduling agreements from purchase scheduling agreements; they solve related but opposite sides of the customer-supplier relationship.
We verify which forecast, JIT and planning delivery-schedule capabilities apply to the target deployment.
When we integrate external buyer schedules, we design message identity, cumulative-quantity reconciliation and error recovery as part of the process.
lead_questions: Do we need separate call-off orders, or does the customer send a rolling delivery schedule?
Which delivery schedule owns the operational demand: forecast, JIT or planning?
How do we reconcile cumulative quantities between buyer and supplier?
How does a schedule line become delivery due?
How do we recover when an external delivery schedule is missing, duplicated or inconsistent?
